setup: Lie back on an incline bench set to roughly 30-45 degrees with a barbell racked above the chest.
commonMistakes: Setting incline too steep, shifting load to shoulders
Bouncing bar off chest
Flaring elbows to 90 degrees

setup: Lie face down on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging below shoulders.
commonMistakes: Using momentum to swing weights up
Shrugging shoulders instead of squeezing shoulder blades
Bending elbows too much, turning it into a row

formCues: Sit on incline bench facing away
setup: Sit on an incline bench positioned between two low cable pulleys, handles gripped at chest height.
commonMistakes: Leaning too far forward off the bench
Not pressing through full range
Letting elbows flare excessively

formCues: Hands form diamond shape on bench edge
setup: Place hands in a diamond shape on an elevated bench with feet on the floor in a plank position.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag
Flaring elbows out wide
Not achieving full range of motion

formCues: Lower with control to chest level
setup: Lie back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level.
commonMistakes: Letting dumbbells drift too far forward or back
Using too steep an incline
Not controlling the eccentric

setup: Sit back against an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms fully extended below the shoulders.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows drift forward
Using momentum to swing the weight
Not fully extending arms at the bottom

formCues: Lower arms wide until stretch felt
setup: Lie on an incline bench with dumbbells pressed above the chest, palms facing each other.
commonMistakes: Bending elbows too much, turning it into a press
Lowering too deep and straining shoulders
Using excessive weight

setup: Sit back against an incline bench with dumbbells held at the sides in a neutral grip.
commonMistakes: Swinging the weight with momentum
Letting elbows travel forward
Rushing the eccentric phase

formCues: Lie face down on incline bench
setup: Lie face down on a steep incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand hanging below the shoulders.
commonMistakes: Rolling shoulders instead of shrugging vertically
Using momentum instead of controlled contraction
Not achieving full range at the top

formCues: Lie on incline bench holding EZ-bar overhead
setup: Lie back on an incline bench holding an EZ-bar with arms extended above the chest.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows flare outward
Moving upper arms during the rep
Lowering the bar too far toward the neck

formCues: Adjust seat so handles align with upper chest
setup: Sit in the incline chest press machine with back against the pad and hands gripping the handles at chest level.
commonMistakes: Seat height set too low or high
Using partial range of motion
Lifting hips off the seat

formCues: Lie face down on incline bench
Raise arms in a Y shape overhead
setup: Lie face down on an incline bench with light dumbbells hanging below in a Y position.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and losing form
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears
Not raising arms high enough

formCues: Push through palms to extend arms
setup: Place hands on an elevated surface like a bench with feet on the ground in a plank position.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag or pike up
Flaring elbows out too wide
Not lowering far enough

formCues: Secure feet at top of incline bench
setup: Lie back on an incline sit-up bench with feet hooked under the pads at the top.
commonMistakes: Yanking the neck to generate momentum
Using too steep an incline before ready
Not controlling the descent

formCues: Keep body straight from head to heels
setup: Lie under a fixed bar or in a suspension trainer, gripping the bar with body straight and heels on the ground.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag
Not pulling chest fully to the bar
Using momentum instead of controlled pulling

formCues: Arms extended straight out to sides on rings
setup: Support the body on gymnastic rings or straps with arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
commonMistakes: Attempting without sufficient shoulder strength
Letting arms bend under fatigue
Arching or sagging the torso

formCues: Climb with alternating hands and feet
setup: Step onto the angled ladder-climbing machine and begin climbing at a self-paced rate.
commonMistakes: Gripping handrails too tightly and taking weight off legs
Climbing at an unsustainable pace early
Slouching forward instead of staying upright

formCues: Roll spine down vertebra by vertebra
setup: Stand on a raised platform holding a light barbell or dumbbell in front of the thighs.
commonMistakes: Using too much load for a spinal flexion movement
Rushing the segmental roll
Bending knees to compensate

formCues: One hand pronated, one supinated grip
setup: Straddle a loaded barbell on the floor with one foot forward and one hand gripping in front, one behind.
commonMistakes: Uneven weight distribution between sides
Twisting the spine during the pull
Not alternating stance and grip between sets

setup: Stand under a pull-up bar within jumping reach, gripping the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
commonMistakes: Muscling through with arms alone instead of using the jump
Failing to transition elbows over the bar smoothly
Kipping excessively and losing control

setup: Lift a loaded keg and hold it hugged tightly against the chest with both arms wrapped around it.
commonMistakes: Letting the keg slip away from the chest
Rounding the back during the lift
Walking too fast and losing control

setup: Load a keg onto one shoulder with the supporting arm wrapped over the top, standing upright.
commonMistakes: Leaning excessively to one side
Not bracing the core before walking
Rushing the initial lift onto the shoulder

formCues: Hinge at hips to grip keg
setup: Stand facing a raised bar with a keg on the ground between the feet, gripping it low with both hands.
commonMistakes: Lifting with the back instead of hips and legs
Poor timing on the release
Standing too close or far from the bar

setup: Stand holding a kettlebell in one hand at waist height, ready to pass it around the body.
commonMistakes: Losing grip during hand-offs
Leaning excessively to compensate
Rushing the pace and losing control

formCues: Hold kettlebell upside down by handle
setup: Grip a kettlebell by the handle with the bell pointing up and walk forward while stabilizing the wrist.
commonMistakes: Letting the kettlebell tip over from grip fatigue
Gripping too loosely
Shrugging the shoulder to compensate for instability

setup: Stand over a kettlebell with a hip hinge, gripping the handle ready to pull it to a bottoms-up rack position.
commonMistakes: Letting the kettlebell flop over instead of stabilizing it
Using too much weight for wrist strength
Pulling with the arm instead of the hips

formCues: Start with bell inverted at shoulder
setup: Hold a kettlebell upside down at shoulder height with the bell pointing toward the ceiling.
commonMistakes: Allowing the bell to tip during the press
Leaning back to generate momentum
Gripping too loosely and losing stability

formCues: Hinge and pull kettlebell close to body
setup: Stand with a kettlebell on the ground between the feet, gripping it with a hip hinge.
commonMistakes: Letting the bell swing away from the body, causing wrist impact
Pulling with the arm instead of hip extension
Catching the rack position too stiffly

setup: Clean a kettlebell to the rack position at the shoulder before initiating the jerk drive overhead.
commonMistakes: Pressing instead of using leg drive for the jerk
Poor rack position before the dip
Not locking out fully overhead

setup: Clean a kettlebell to the shoulder rack position, then press it overhead in a controlled motion.
commonMistakes: Using momentum from the clean to cheat the press
Leaning back excessively during the press
Losing rack position before pressing

setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor between the feet.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back
Squatting the movement instead of hinging
Not fully extending hips at the top

setup: Hold a kettlebell in each hand at the sides while rising up onto the toes before walking.
commonMistakes: Dropping heels down during the walk
Letting shoulders round forward
Taking overly long strides and losing balance

setup: Grip a kettlebell in each hand at the sides, standing tall before walking forward.
commonMistakes: Letting shoulders slump forward
Walking too fast and losing posture
Leaning to one side with uneven loads

formCues: Pass kettlebell between legs in figure-8 pattern
setup: Stand in a quarter squat with a kettlebell in one hand, ready to pass it between the legs in a figure-8.
commonMistakes: Standing too upright, limiting range of motion
Losing grip during hand-offs between legs
Rounding the back during the pass

setup: Stand in a quarter squat, passing the kettlebell in a figure-8 between the legs before catching it in a hold.
commonMistakes: Fumbling the catch at the end of the pattern
Losing hip hinge position during the pass
Rushing the transition to the hold

formCues: Lie on back with knees bent
Keep elbow close to body at bottom
setup: Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding a kettlebell at shoulder height in one hand.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbow out at the bottom of the press
Arching the back off the floor excessively
Losing control of the kettlebell path

formCues: Press kettlebell overhead while lying down
Sit up while keeping arm locked
Move through the pattern with control
setup: Lie on the back holding a kettlebell pressed overhead in one arm with the same-side knee bent.
commonMistakes: Bending the pressing arm during the sit-up
Rushing the transition instead of moving deliberately
Losing visual focus on the kettlebell

setup: Hold a kettlebell vertically against the chest with both hands cupping the horns.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward
Rounding the upper back
Not reaching adequate squat depth

formCues: Hinge over two kettlebells on floor
setup: Stand hinged over two kettlebells on the floor, gripping one handle in each hand.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back during the hinge
Rotating the torso excessively while rowing
Using momentum instead of a controlled pull

formCues: Hold kettlebell upside down at chest
setup: Hold a kettlebell by the horns upside down at chest level, ready to circle it around the head.
commonMistakes: Arching the back to let the bell pass behind the head
Moving too fast and losing control
Letting elbows flare excessively
